/-!
# Conjecture 1.6

by L. A. Bokut'

(A. I. Mal'cev). Is the group ring of a right-ordered group embeddable into a
skew field?

A right-ordered group is a group $G$ with a total order $<$ that is invariant
under right multiplication: $a < b$ implies $ac < bc$ for all $a, b, c \in G$.
A skew field is a division ring, not necessarily commutative. "Embeddable"
means that there is an injective ring homomorphism.

The notebook does not name the coefficient ring. We follow the classical
reading of Mal'cev's problem and ask the question for the group ring $K[G]$
over every field $K$. (For $K = \mathbb{Q}$ this is equivalent to the question
for the integral group ring $\mathbb{Z}[G]$.)

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

claims.decomposer_note: Single yes/no question with an implicit universal quantifier over all right-ordered groups G (groups with a total order invariant under right multiplication); 'the group ring' leaves the coefficient ring implicit (the classical reading is the group ring K[G] over an arbitrary field K, or equivalently the integral group ring ℤ[G] for the ℚ-case), 'skew field' means a division ring (not necessarily commutative), and 'embeddable' means the existence of an injective ring homomorphism; the formalization should fix and document the coefficient convention (e.g. quantify over all fields K, or use ℤ[G]) and use `answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ G ..., ∃ division ring D, ∃ injective ring hom K[G] → D`.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state the same proposition (answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ field K, ∀ right-ordered group G, ∃ division ring D, ∃ injective ring hom MonoidAlgebra K G →+* D). Chose the c02/c05 form using `MulRightStrictMono G` (a < b → a*c < b*c), the literal textbook right-order axiom; it is equivalent to the `MulRightMono` form used by c01/c03/c04/c06/c07/c08 in a linearly ordered group (right multiplication is a bijection), so no candidate was unfaithful. Kept c05's AMS tags 6 16 20 (ordered groups, associative rings, group theory) and edited the docstrings to document the coefficient convention explicitly.

/-!
# Conjecture 1.6

by L. A. Bokut'

(A. I. Mal'cev). Is the group ring of a right-ordered group embeddable into a

reading of Mal'cev's problem and ask the question for the group ring $K[G]$
over every field $K$. (For $K = \mathbb{Q}$ this is equivalent to the question

namespace Kourovka.«1.6»

/--
(A. I. Mal'cev). Is the group ring of a right-ordered group embeddable into a
skew field?

Precisely: for every field $K$ and every group $G$ with a total order satisfying
$a < b \Rightarrow ac < bc$, is there a division ring $D$ and an injective ring
homomorphism $K[G] \to D$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 6 16 20]
theorem kourovka.«1.6» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (K : Type) [Field K] (G : Type) [Group G] [LinearOrder G] [MulRightStrictMono G],
      ∃ (D : Type) (_ : DivisionRing D) (f : MonoidAlgebra K G →+* D),
        Function.Injective f := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«1.6»

items: Coefficient ring: the notebook says only 'the group ring'. Following the classical reading of Mal'cev's problem (and the decomposition notes), the statement quantifies over all fields K (coefficients in an arbitrary field). This is at least as strong as the ℤ[G] reading (ℤ[G] ⊂ ℚ[G]); a reading with division-ring coefficients would be stronger still and was not chosen. Documented in the module and theorem docstrings.

Right-ordered group is modelled as `[Group G] [LinearOrder G] [MulRightStrictMono G]`, i.e. a total order with a < b → a*c < b*c (invariance under right multiplication), matching the literal 'right-ordered'. Since the group ring depends only on G and right-orderability is equivalent to left-orderability, the left/right convention does not affect the truth value.

Universe levels: K, G and the target skew field D are all taken in `Type`, following the idiom of the other Kourovka files (e.g. 1_40, 1_74). Any embedding into a division ring in a higher universe can be cut down to the (small) division closure of the image, so this loses no generality.
'Embeddable' is rendered as the existence of an injective ring homomorphism `MonoidAlgebra K G →+* D`; Mathlib has no bundled ring-embedding structure or 'embeds in a division ring' predicate.
AMS tags 6 (ordered algebraic structures), 16 (associative rings), 20 (group theory).

reviewer_notes: Ambiguity in the source: 'the group ring' does not name the coefficient ring. Following the decomposition notes and the standard reading of Mal'cev's problem in the literature (K[G] over a field), the final statement quantifies over all fields K; this subsumes the ℤ[G]/ℚ[G] reading (ℤ[G] embeds in a division ring iff ℚ[G] does) but is strictly stronger if some prime-characteristic case failed. This is documented in the module and theorem docstrings. Right-ordered group is modelled as a group carrying a fixed LinearOrder with MulRightStrictMono (literal 'right-ordered', not 'right-orderable'; the conclusion does not depend on the order so the readings coincide). Skew field = DivisionRing (possibly noncommutative); embeddable = injective unital ring hom. All types in `Type`, following the Kourovka directory convention. Sanity: trivial group is right-ordered and K[1] ≅ K embeds, so hypotheses are satisfiable; answer(True)/answer(False) correspond to positive/negative answers. No omissions; all candidates compiled and reported the slot as formalized with no objections to the decomposition.
